task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 5, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update about a new fee arrangement at the fictional Kestrel Bend public market and why different vendors expect different effects.

facts.text: Kestrel Bend's nine-member market board voted 7-2 on Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026, to replace its flat weekly stall fee.
Beginning Sept. 1, regular vendors will pay $18 a week plus 5% of gross market sales instead of a flat $30.
For a vendor with $100 in weekly sales, the new fee is $23; for one with $300, it is $33.
The market has 46 regular vendors selling produce, prepared food, flowers and household crafts.
A separate daily fee for occasional guest stalls will remain $15.
Vendors will report sales themselves on a weekly form; the board has not adopted an electronic payment requirement.
Market director Tessa Rook said existing records show only stall occupancy, so the board cannot yet predict each vendor's new bill.
The market's operating deficit was $28,000 in the last fiscal year, largely reflecting a roof repair and higher cleaning costs.
The city covered that deficit with a one-time appropriation and has not promised another subsidy.
The board will review six months of fee receipts before deciding whether to keep the sales-based system.
Flower seller Oona Drel said her weekly sales vary sharply with weather and event bookings.
Drel said, "A quieter week should not cost me the same as a full table of orders."
Hot-food vendor Silas Gant said gross sales do not account for his ingredient and refrigeration costs.
Gant said, "The board sees the sale, but it does not see what I paid to put that meal together."
The board defines the percentage base as sales made at this market before business expenses, excluding separately collected sales tax; sales elsewhere are not included.
Two dissenting board members sought a fee cap; the adopted measure contains none.
The board also approved free bookkeeping help through a local nonprofit, beginning with four September sessions.
The fee vote did not change the market's Saturday opening hours or its winter calendar.
The market began in a former tram shed in 1998 and still uses movable stalls rather than permanent shop units.
No vendor has given the board a formal departure notice since the vote; that does not establish that all intend to stay.

forbidden_additions: Every vendor will pay less or the board has verified vendors' profits
A fee cap or required electronic checkout absent from the adopted measure
